Author: Joel Moss <joel@developwithstyle.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 5 12:33:30 2026 +0100

    feat(macapp): frame the focused workroom pane
    
    The focused member of a workroom split was signalled only by its fill — accent @ 0.10
    over a `panel` that is itself 5.5% off the theme background — plus a slightly stronger
    shadow. That moves luminance by a couple of percent, which is not enough to pick the
    focused workroom out of a split at a glance.
    
    Frame the card instead: `WorkroomPaneCardBorder` strokes the card at 1.5pt, and its
    COLOUR carries focus — the accent on the focused member, a neutral `border` hairline on
    the rest, and `focused` (fg @ 0.3) when the window isn't key, so a background window
    never holds a saturated accent. The accent fill stays as the secondary cue.
    
    1.5pt at radius 8 matches the terminal pane's focus ring rather than the 2pt accent box
    of the drag drop-edge highlight, so a focused pane can't be mistaken for a drop target.
    The stroke is always mounted and only its colour swaps — no `_ConditionalContent` branch
    beside the leaf's content slot. Mounted after the clip and before the shadow;
    `strokeBorder` insets by half its width, so nothing about the layout changes.

# Highlight the focused workroom pane only inside a split

## Context

`56d1dc73` made the focused split member's cue a 1.5pt accent frame on the pane card, on top of the
existing accent-tinted fill and stronger shadow. All three are keyed on the leaf's `focused` Bool.

A **solo** workroom is rendered through the same path — `AppStore.visibleWorkroomLayout(for:)`
returns `.leaf(selected)`, so the single leaf's `sid == focusedID` and `focused` is *always* true.
The lone pane therefore wears the full focused treatment: accent frame, accent fill, strong shadow.
That's a selection cue with nothing to select *among* — there is no peer to distinguish it from, so
it reads as decoration and spends the accent that should mean "this one, not that one".

Outcome: the card's focus treatment becomes split-only. A solo workroom is the **neutral resting
card** (neutral hairline frame, plain raised fill, light shadow). Its **header is untouched** —
accent glyph, primary text, full-opacity Run / Open-in controls — because dimming the only pane's
own actions would be a regression, and `TargetTerminalDetail(surfaceActive:)` must stay on `focused`
(it's liveness, not emphasis).

| | frame | fill | shadow | header |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| solo | `border` | `splitGroupFill` | 0.10 / r3 | accent glyph, primary text, controls @ 1.0 |
| split, focused | `accent` | `splitGroupFocusedFill` | 0.18 / r6 | same as solo |
| split, unfocused | `border` | `splitGroupFill` | 0.10 / r3 | `fgMuted` glyph + text, controls @ 0.45 |

(Background window still overrides frame `accent` → `focused` and fill → `splitGroupFill`, unchanged.)

## Implementation

All in `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift`.

### 1. One derived flag, one rule

`multi` is already threaded into `WorkroomPaneLeaf` (`:71`, `:156`) and already gates the
`.isSelected` trait with this exact expression (`:254`) — reuse that precedent, don't add new
plumbing to `WorkroomSplitView`.

Add the rule beside the existing pure `tint` on `WorkroomPaneCardBorder` (`:338-341`), which is
already non-private for tests and is the primary cue:

```swift
/// Whether the card wears the focused treatment at all. Model focus alone isn't enough: a solo pane
/// is always `focused` (the no-split layout is `.leaf(selected)`), and an accent frame/fill with no
/// peer to be distinguished FROM is decoration, not a selection cue. Same expression the
/// `.isSelected` trait uses, kept pure so the gate is testable without hosting a view.
static func isHighlighted(focused: Bool, multi: Bool) -> Bool { focused && multi }
```

In `WorkroomPaneLeaf`, derive it once (private computed var, beside `projectPath`/`toolbarControls`)
and feed **all three** card cues from it — `focused` keeps driving the title bar and
`TargetTerminalDetail(surfaceActive:)`:

```swift
private var highlighted: Bool {
  WorkroomPaneCardBorder.isHighlighted(focused: focused, multi: multi)
}
```

- `:234` → `.background(WorkroomPaneCardBackground(highlighted: highlighted))`
- `:239` → `.overlay { WorkroomPaneCardBorder(highlighted: highlighted) }`
- `:240-242` shadow → `focused ? …` becomes `highlighted ? …`

### 2. Rename the axis in the two child views

Rename the stored property `focused` → `highlighted` in `WorkroomPaneCardBackground` (`:292-304`)
and `WorkroomPaneCardBorder` (`:315-342`), and `tint`'s first label `focused:` → `highlighted:`.
The name has to change: these views no longer mean "is the model-focused pane", they mean "wears the
focused treatment", and leaving the old label would make the solo case read as a bug at every call
site. Also retarget `WorkroomPaneCardBorder`'s `.animation(…, value: focused)` (`:328`) to
`highlighted`, so a 2-member split dissolving to solo cross-fades accent → hairline.

`WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (`:386-488`) is **not** touched — it keeps `focused`.

**Preserve both structural invariants**: the stroke and the fill stay *unconditionally mounted* with
only their colour swapping (no `_ConditionalContent` branch beside the leaf's content slot — the
blank/stranded-pane hazard the file's `:164-176` comment exists for), and `strokeBorder`'s half-width
inset keeps every pane rect identical. This change only moves the values fed in.

### 3. Comments that are now false

- `:227-233` — the card-styling block comment ends "Both are unconditional since issue #139 — a solo
  pane is always the focused one, so it takes the accent treatment with no special case." That is
  exactly the behaviour being reversed. Rewrite: unconditional *mounting* is preserved, but the
  treatment is now split-only, and say why (accent means "this member, not that one").
- `:287-291` and `:306-314` — the two view docs describe the axis as focus; restate as the
  highlighted axis and keep the `\.controlActiveState`-in-a-child rationale verbatim (it's about
  keeping activation re-renders off the libghostty surface, still load-bearing).
- `:376-381` — `WorkroomPaneTitleBar`'s doc still accurate; leave it.

### 4. Tests

`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomSplitTests.swift`, the `// MARK: pane card frame` section
(`:759-790`) — reuse the existing `frameTokens` fixture:

- Update the three existing `tint` tests to the `highlighted:` label (names/docs already read
  "focused member", which stays true for the split case).
- Add gate tests: `isHighlighted(focused: true, multi: false) == false` (solo — the regression this
  change fixes, asserting `tint` of that result is `tokens.border`), `(true, true) == true`,
  `(false, true) == false`.

No XCUITest change: colours and strokes aren't visible to XCUITest, and the one
accessibility-visible focus signal (`.isSelected`, `:254`) is already gated on `focused && multi`,
so its behaviour is unchanged by this work.

## Verification

```bash
make app-format && make app-lint       # hard gate
make app-test                          # needs dangerouslyDisableSandbox
```

`make app-test` hides its summary under Xcode 26 — read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` with
`xcresulttool`, not from stdout.

Then `make app-run` and look at it:

1. Open a project, select a single workroom → card has a faint neutral hairline, plain raised fill,
   light shadow. **No accent anywhere on the card edge.** Header still bright: accent cube glyph,
   full-strength `project / workroom` text, crisp Run / Open-in buttons.
2. Drag a second workroom tab onto the pane to split → the focused member picks up the accent frame
   + accent fill + deeper shadow; the other goes hairline/plain with its header muted to 0.45.
3. Click between the two members → the frame swaps accent ⟷ hairline over 0.08s.
4. ✕ one member back out to solo → the surviving pane drops to the neutral card (cross-faded), and
   its terminal is not re-parented (no blank pane, scrollback intact).
5. ⌘Tab to another app with a split open → the focused member's frame goes neutral `focused`
   (fg @ 0.3), not accent. With a solo workroom, activation changes nothing on the card.

`visibleWorkroomLayout(for:)` returns `.leaf(selected)`, so the single leaf's
`sid == focusedID` and `focused` is ALWAYS true. The lone pane therefore wore the
full focused treatment: accent frame, accent-tinted fill, deeper shadow. That's a
selection cue with nothing to select among, so it read as decoration and spent the
accent that should mean "this member, not that one".

Gate the card's treatment on `multi` instead. `WorkroomPaneCardBorder.isHighlighted`
holds the rule (`focused && multi` — the same expression the `.isSelected` trait
already used), the leaf derives it ONCE, and the frame, the fill and the shadow all
read that one value so they can't disagree about it. Solo is now the neutral resting
card: `border` hairline, `splitGroupFill`, shadow 0.10/r3 — identical to an unfocused
member.

`focused` still drives the title bar and `TargetTerminalDetail(surfaceActive:)`. That
axis is liveness, not emphasis: muting the only pane's own Run / Open-in controls
would be a regression, and its terminal stays active. So a solo pane keeps its accent
glyph, full-strength label and full-opacity controls above a neutral card.

Both layers stay unconditionally MOUNTED and only their values swap — the treatment,
not the mounting, is what's split-only, so no `_ConditionalContent` branch appears
beside the leaf's content slot and no pane rect moves.
